sources.entry: seb-mac - Safe Exam Browser for macOS and iOS.

summary.one_liner: Open source code base for Safe Exam Browser (SEB), a locked-down browser for macOS and iOS used for computer-based exams, plus the SEB Verificator macOS app.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes this as the open source Xcode code base for Safe Exam Browser on macOS and iOS, with a SEB Verificator macOS target. It states that main reflects SEB for macOS/iOS 3.3.2 or newer and that the project is a unified macOS/iOS/iPadOS Xcode workspace containing both macOS and iOS targets and a SEBVerificator target. It notes that the SEB Alliance contributors' binary security modules and Zoom integration (proprietary licenses) are not included, so some references must be removed to build. It also says the code is mainly for educational purposes and building custom SEB versions requires consulting SEB Alliance Platinum or Diamond contributors. Documentation lives in other repositories, per the README.
use_cases: running computer-based exams on iOS or iPadOS
studying the source of a secure exam browser
verifying SEB configurations with SEB Verificator
reviewing Xcode project structure for a multi-platform Apple app
how_to_run: Install a recent version of Xcode (README says currently 14.3.1).
Add your own code signing identities.
Request the com.apple.developer.edu-assessment-mode entitlement from Apple for your developer team.
Remove missing references to proprietary components before building.
notable: Unified Xcode workspace with macOS and iOS targets plus a SEBVerificator target
Uses Apple's edu-assessment-mode entitlement on iOS
Proprietary security modules and Zoom integration are excluded from the open source code
README sets a spelling rule: SEB in all caps in user-facing text
caveats: Binary security modules and Zoom integration are not included, so the project will not build as-is without edits.
Building customized SEB versions requires consulting SEB Alliance Platinum or Diamond contributors; the code is mainly for educational use.
Building for iOS with Xcode 15.x breaks the custom SEB user agent in UIWebView, per the README.
